newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers protest for better work conditions.
newsitem.headline: French truckers protest for better work conditions.

text.p: French truckers snarled traffic, stopped work and protested across the country on Monday to press their demands for more money and shorter working hours.

The Workers Force (FO) trade union said a delegation of protesters would seek a meeting with a government official later in the day to spell out grievances. Unions want wage rises, shorter working hours and the right to retire at 55 not 60.
It was France's second road transport protest this month.
Police reported traffic congestion around the southwestern town of Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor, truck drivers blocked the three main access roads to the city.

Protesters cut off a bridge connecting France and Germany over the river Rhine at Strasbourg. There were roadblocks near several other major cities including Marseille in the south, Caen, Le Mans and Rennes in the west, and Troyes in the east.

In Toulouse motorists had a free motorway ride as protesters lifted toll gates. The winter's first snowfall worsened disruption in the Lyon and Valence areas. Other drivers stopped work leaving their trucks outside haulage companies.
Traffic was disrupted earlier in several cities by demonstrators demanding cuts in taxes on diesel fuel.
Haulage company bosses snarled traffic in several cities 10 days ago and won a government pledge to keep down increases in taxes on diesel fuel.
